lessons.title: Iqlab (conversion)
lessons.lede: Turning noon sakinah or tanween into a hidden meem before baa (ب), keeping the ghunnah.

idea.lead: When baa (ب) comes after noon sakinah or tanween, the noon is pronounced as a meem, though it is not written as one, and that meem is then hidden before the baa, with ghunnah.
idea.kidsLead: When baa (ب) comes after a noon sakinah or tanween, we say the noon as a meem, and keep the humming sound from the nose for two counts.

how.text: The noon or tanween is pronounced as a meem, but not written as one.
The meem is hidden before the baa: neither pronounced clearly nor merged.
The nasal sound comes from the nose, for two counts.

idea.note: Reciters differ on how the lips close in iqlab, so learn how it is done from your teacher, by listening and reciting.

ayat.findHint: Find where iqlab happens in each ayah, then bring the colours back to check.

why: Noon sakinah + baa in one word
Noon sakinah + baa across two words

ayat.tip: In the Mushaf, iqlab is marked by a small meem above the noon, or in place of the second vowel mark of the tanween, as you can see in the ayahs above.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the noon sakinah in:
quiz.why: Baa comes after the noon sakinah, so the noon turns into a hidden meem, with ghunnah.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the tanween in:
quiz.why: Tanween follows the rules of noon sakinah. Baa comes after it, so it turns into a hidden meem.
Iqlab has one letter only: baa.

quiz.q: In iqlab, the noon turns into which letter?
quiz.why: The noon is pronounced as a meem, and that meem is then hidden before the baa.
In «أَنۢبِئْهُم», baa comes after the noon sakinah. «مِن قَبْلُ» has ikhfa', «مِنْ هَادٍ» has izhar, and «مَن يَقُولُ» has idgham with ghunnah.

quiz.q: How is iqlab marked in the Mushaf?
options: A small meem above the noon
quiz.why: A small meem is written above the noon, or in place of the second vowel mark of the tanween.

quiz.q: How long is the ghunnah in iqlab?
quiz.why: The ghunnah in iqlab lasts two counts, as in ikhfa'.

lessons.title: Ikhfa' (concealment)
lessons.lede: Pronouncing noon sakinah or tanween in a state between izhar and idgham, without a shaddah, keeping the ghunnah.

formula.caption: letters that may come after it

idea.lead: When one of the fifteen letters comes after noon sakinah or tanween, you neither pronounce the noon clearly nor merge it: you say it in a state between the two.
idea.kidsLead: When one of the fifteen letters comes after noon sakinah or tanween, we hide the noon: we don't say it clearly and don't merge it into the next letter, and we keep the humming sound from the nose for two counts.

how.text: It gets ready for the next letter's point of articulation, without touching the point of the noon.
The nasal sound comes from the nose, for two counts.
There is no shaddah here; this is what tells ikhfa' apart from idgham.

idea.note: The ghunnah is heavy before ص ض ط ظ ق, and light before the other ten letters.

ayat.findHint: Find where ikhfa' happens in each ayah, then bring the colours back to check.
ayat.tip: A hint from the script: in many Mushafs the hidden noon is written without a sukun, as you can see in the ayahs above.

letters.title: The fifteen letters
letters.hint: The first letter of each word in this well-known line of verse is one of the letters of ikhfa'.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the noon sakinah in:
quiz.why: Qaaf is one of the fifteen letters of ikhfa', so the noon is hidden, with ghunnah. The ghunnah is heavy, because qaaf is an elevated (heavy) letter.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the noon sakinah in:
quiz.why: Haa (ه) is a throat letter, so the noon is pronounced clearly, without hiding or merging: this is izhar.
Sheen is one of the letters of ikhfa'. «مَن يَقُولُ» has idgham with ghunnah, «مِن بَعْدِ» has iqlab, and «مِنْ هَادٍ» has izhar.

quiz.q: How long is the ghunnah in ikhfa'?
quiz.why: The ghunnah in ikhfa' lasts two counts; one count is about the time it takes to fold or unfold a finger.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the noon sakinah in:
quiz.why: Before baa, the noon turns into a hidden meem, with ghunnah: this is iqlab.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the noon sakinah in:
quiz.why: Yaa is one of the letters of «يَنْمُو», so the noon merges into it with ghunnah.

quiz.q: What is the rule for the tanween in:
quiz.why: Tanween follows the rules of noon sakinah. Saad is one of the letters of ikhfa', and the ghunnah is heavy with it, because saad is an elevated (heavy) letter.
